A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WORFBENCH/WORFEVAL study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning and held-out generalization results, downstream task performance, execution-time analyses, and o1 case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds quantitative o1-preview evaluation, a gold-node-chain ablation, and analysis of test-graph topological orders.

M1.justification: The workflow construction, quality filtering, Sentence-BERT matching, LIS/MCIS scoring, and downstream workflow procedures remain unchanged. The gold-chain experiment is an evaluation control, and the 20-order evaluation cap already appears in v1.

E1.justification: All dataset sources, four application domains, held-out datasets, and downstream benchmarks remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds a limited edge-only test scenario in which gold node chains are supplied, changing the required prediction task and available input information within the existing data.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds o1-preview to the quantitative benchmark comparison; v1 includes o1 only in case studies. The other comparator memberships in the main, generalization, and downstream comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new ablation supplies gold node chains and evaluates only dependency prediction, using two-shot prompting across eight selected models. Existing prompting, decoding temperature, semantic threshold, training hyperparameters, and the 20-topological-order cap are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4/Table 5 adds a systematic controlled ablation across four domains that separates node-generation errors from dependency-prediction difficulty, substantially strengthening the diagnostic analysis. Appendix A.9/Table 7 additionally examines topological-order counts to justify the existing evaluation cap. Earlier error analyses and o1 cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. v3 continues point-estimate reporting; its new topological-order frequencies are descriptive results rather than a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial controlled results: supplying gold chains yields average graph F1 of 74.63 for GPT-4 versus 52.47 without them, and Table 7 reports that 96.01% of test graphs have at most 20 topological orders. Table 1 adds o1-preview at 66.70/51.63 average chain/graph F1 and replaces Claude's 63.70/46.84 with 66.70/52.53. Because v3 specifies a more detailed Claude identifier, these replacements do not establish same-checkpoint gains. Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.2 newly asserts that the DAG workflows are equivalent in expressivity to Marked Graphs, without supplying a proof or formal construction. The existing DAG formalization and WORFEVAL equations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v3 removes Section 5.3's explicit claim to be the first benchmark for generating complex graph-structured natural-language workflows across multiple scenarios. The principal benchmark, evaluator, planning-gap, and downstream-benefit claims in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion are retained.

C2.justification: The revised limitations explicitly identify missing mixed-action tasks and unsupported choices/loops, replacing the earlier probabilistic-node qualification. Section 3.2 acknowledges possible benefits from prompt optimization and multi-agent architectures instead of its earlier warning about feedback, reinforcement learning, and inference-time scaling. The new ablation also supports a more specific interpretation of residual dependency-prediction errors.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code/data release; v3 states availability and reports submitting test data and evaluation code as supplementary materials. v3 also explicitly identifies LlamaFactory as the training framework and specifies o1-preview and claude-3.5-sonnet-1022. These are reporting/access changes; the retained training hyperparameters and hardware are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands positioning into classical concurrency, Petri nets, process calculi, workflow modeling, and process mining. It adds comparisons with PlanBench, CAT-Bench, and AFlow, introduces prompt-optimization and GPTSwarm references, and removes the explicit first-benchmark claim while pruning broader agent/reasoning citations.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in related work and local experimental discussion. Limitations move from the main document to Appendix A.8, existing appendix sections are renumbered, and affiliation, conference-header, and acknowledgment text is added. The overall narrative and most methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the ablation and topological-order tables, expands and compacts Table 1, and reformats Figure 2's example panel. The training table is renumbered, and appendix placement changes locally. Existing result charts and the general visual organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The gold-chain control strengthens the evidence that dependency prediction remains difficult even with correct subtasks, while Appendix A.9 supplies an empirical rationale for the previously unexplained evaluation cap. Expanded research context, clearer limitations, and improved access documentation also help. These focused gains outweigh minor reporting inconsistencies, including retaining an 18-model total after Table 1 expands to 19 models.
